title: Post-lunch kernel fidget notes
content:
Post-lunch brain dump / quick todo list - kernel-level fidgets

Context: brief oncall handover -> saw p99 spike on r11 around 12:30 PST. Root symptoms: sudden increase in micro-batch latencies, ~15% of requests hit full kv-cache refill path.

Quick timeline (sketch):
- 12:20: deploy of small batching tweak (PR 1987) -> opt-in on r11 only
- 12:27: first warning from tracing (batcher queue growth)
- 12:31: p99 spike (3x usual)
- 12:45: partial mitigation by toggling batching flag back on r11

Immediate checklist (things I want to try before pairing with Maya):
- [ ] Re-run microbench on r11 with synthetic workload that mimics 16->512 token variance (script: tools/microbench/synth-var.sh)
- [ ] Add lightweight debug log for kv-cache hit/miss in serving runtime (only on staging) — avoid full trace to limit overhead
- [ ] Short experiment: force 2-second TTL on secondary-kv entries to observe eviction pressure (small window)
- [ ] Run `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` while simulating the spike and capture hotspots; focus on mutex contention in cache eviction path
- [ ] Check kernel-level counters: aio queues, futex waiters -- are we seeing thread parking storms?

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching change altered arrival distribution -> KV cache saw larger footprint + more concurrent refill -> lock contention (eviction mutex hot)
2) Backpressure/tokens shaping created short bursts that overflow small internal request queue -> dispatcher starts serializing and increases tail latency
3) System-level IO scheduling: some instance had a CPU affinity shift (cron job?) causing CPU starvation for the eviction background thread
4) Rare: clock skew between worker threads making cache TTL checks mis-evaluate -> simultaneous eviction runs (weird but saw before in other stack)

Commands / snippets I expect to use:
- tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | jq '.level,.msg' | grep kv_cache
- ./tools/microbench/run_synth --tokens 16,128,512 --qps 1000 --dur 60 --target r11
- sudo perf top -p $(pgrep runtime) --sort comm
- sudo cat /proc/interrupts | egrep 'nvme|eth'
- taskset -pc <pid>  # check thread pinning (compare to expected cpuset)

Quick notes on instrumentation I want (short-term, cheap):
- lightweight per-shard atomic counters: cache_refills, cache_evictions, refill_latency_ms (buckets)
- tracing tag when refill size > 64 entries (cause: large model context)
- metric: concurrent_refill_workers (gauge) -> alert when > 2 on single host

Observations from the tail logs this morning (scraped):
- `kv_cache: refill started, size=78, missing_prefix=24, src=memfetch` (several lines clustered)
- `batcher: queued_batch_size=1 after 0ms` (weird: batcher expected >1)
- `worker-evict: acquired_eviction_lock, latency_ms=12` (ok individually but concurrent spikes seen)

Experiment plan (short):
- A: reproduce locally with -p r11 config + synthetic jitter -> confirm increased refill concurrency
- B: test a fix: make eviction lock per-shard (finer grained) and measure p99 reduction (staging)
- C: fallback: rate-limit refill workers to 2 per-host as soft throttle, verify user-visible latency impact

Questions for Maya / pairing notes:
- Can we pair 30m tomorrow 10:30 to walk through the refill path? I want to show the perf flame and explain eviction lock design.
- If we add per-shard lock, does that break any invariants in the cache (Ishaan?) -> need quick design check
- Does Dedicated infra run a different IO scheduler config? Might explain instance-specific behavior.

Snippets of design idea (brain dump):
- "clock skew detector" idea: tiny sampled timestamp check across worker threads to detect >100ms drift; if detected, tag traces and avoid concurrent eviction triggers for X seconds. Cheap guard, might reduce pathological simultaneous runs.
- "eviction slow start": when refill rate jumps > threshold, sequentialize first N refills (serialize on a per-model basis) then ramp concurrency up if latency stable. This would add backpressure into the refill path rather than letting it run wild.

Follow-ups and owners:
- Zeke: prototype per-shard lock in local build (due EOD) -> PR draft if reproducible
- Ishaan: quick check if any recent kube node upgrades changed cpuset/cpu manager config on r11 nodes (asked in slack)
- Maya: pair on refill trace and perf flame (tomorrow 10:30)

Notes to self (do not forget):
- Keep debug logs gated behind env var `RW_KV_DEBUG=1` and always sample 1/100 to avoid noise in staging.
- When measuring perf, always collect `numa_maps` and `taskset` to correlate with thread placement.

Random mental heap (short):
- Might be worth adding a small histogram metric for refill batch sizes (1..128) — we've been blind to distribution shifts.
- Consider a canary on r11 with a stretched TTL to see if reduced evictions correlate with lower p99

End-of-scratchpad quick status:
- Priority: reproduce -> add counters -> test per-shard lock -> pair with Maya.
- Timeboxed: 2h today on repro + perf capture.

-- Zeke
(quick id: post-lunch fidget, not polished, record of flow & next actions)
